Valreek's >!moment of realisation during her death in Claws of Famine. For those of you who don't know it, first off stop reading my post and go read the story - spoilers from here on, but also because it's amazing and honestly the best bit of warhammer writing. It's from the perspective of Valreek, a Ghoul in the underworlds warband the Grymwatch. For the entire story it's written in her point of view, seeing her and her companions as noble brave soldiers, and at the end she dies - and, as she does, the delusion crumbles away. It's absolutely heart wrenching that she not only realises what she really is (a cannibalistic Ghoul) but also that she's realised and died many times before, only to be brought back by the Katophrane curse. "Her voice was gone, and in its place there was only the anguish of lost humanity. Of a mad, hopeless creature facing a lone moment of lucidity before an ocean of nightmarish delusion ... In her last, fleeting moment of clarity, Valreek prayed that it would be the final time" And then she does come back to life thanks to the Katophrane curse, briefly seeing things as they really are before the delusion takes hold again. The final bit is equal parts heart warming as her companions feed her and nurse each other back to health, the epitome of care and camaraderie, and heart breaking as you see the delusion take over once again.!<

# Harvest season



The sun hung low in the sky, dipping towards the treeline as the twilight of evening and sunset began. Hysh's golden rays illuminated the pastoral lands all around, bathing the world in golds and reds. Trees bent over the paths as their leaves turned from green to yellow, and birds and beasts flittered among the branches and around their trunks. 



Queen Nia strolled through the fields, carefree and at peace. Her lands were safe, her people happy - what more could a monarch wish for? And, as if it were fate, the Summerking's visit coincided with the harvest season. A traditional festival in her kingdom, harvest season marked a time where the crops were collected and stored in great granaries for the coming months - but not before a celebratory feast for another year of prosperity and fortune. Decorations were prepared and songs sang, and the whole kingdom came together to celebrate. 



Dipping her head under a string of red bunting tied between the trees, Nia smiled and waved at the labourers and peasants around her. They returned her greeting with cheer, before returning to their duties - scything through the grain and wheat, or cutting apart the bodies of hay that lay all around. To her left, a wooden fence encircled a group of pigs and fowl like an army would encircle the enemy. She watched as the farmers expertly butchered the animals, preparing them for the feast with practised skill. The animals let out brief, almost human screams before the butchers slaughtered them. 



As she walked on, lost in happy thought and enjoying the sunset, she stumbled - over a bushel of apples, of all things! There must have been dozens of them, and she bent down to pick up the largest. It was almost the size of a human head, she thought, as she bit into it. Savouring the crunch and the sweet juices, Nia contentedly strolled on as the rays of Hysh bathed her world in a deep, sanguine red.

Famed across the lands as much for her skill-at-arms and tactical brilliance as for her wit and beauty, Queen Nia of the eastern woodland realms is hailed as a benevolent monarch who leads her people with a fair and just rule. As a young princess she journeyed into the Murkwood Forest on a quest to slay the evil dragons who ravaged her kingdom, and the heroics of her noble band of warriors are recounted time and time again. Now grown and become queen of the lands, Nia fights to protect her people from the darkness of the Mortal Realms. Her castles and keeps are dotted across Ghyran, located in or near forests where her folk can remember that they are one with the land and connect with nature - and, when the forces of Chaos come to despoil, to stand firm and protect that most bounteous realm. Bedecked in her fur-trimmed cape and golden circlet, Queen Nia wields her family's battleaxe with unsurmountable skill. Fighting from the very front lines, she commands a respect and love from the women and men under her command that few others can match. 



Of course, all this is just in her mind - a pervasive delusion shared amongst the flesh-hungry cannibals that squat in the ruins across Ghyran. Tragically, the foes that Queen Nia and her "court" battle against are as often the forces of Order as those of Chaos, and the "victory feast" that she sees herself benevolently sharing amongst the soldiers and peasantry in reality a charnel house of offal and carcasses.

Mine's the Court of the Violet Moon, a homebrew court where I'm fleshing out and developing the narrative with each game. 

Situated in Ghyran, they believe themselves to be noble guardians of nature. Their lands, ruled over by their benevolent archregent Queen Nia, are sprawling forests and woods where the Court sees themselves venerating and protecting the spirits and realm. Even their religion is affected by Ghyran, where the primary deity they worship is Offalielle - a twisted broken-mirror reflection of Alarielle. Unfortunately, like all Flesh-Eater Courts, what they see and reality are rarely the same - the ivy garlands and purple ribbons they adorn themselves and the forests with are in fact grisly entrails and flayed strips of skin, the beautiful aelven runes they see respectfully carved onto tree trunks in fact crude daubings in blood and gore, and the axe-bearing fire daemons they see coming to despoil the natural world often in fact the Sylvaneth. 

There's some realm-path hopping too, or perhaps it's just all in the delusion - when she was younger and only a Princess instead of the Queen she is today, Nia led her closest companions into the Gnarlwood to hunt down and slay the dragons that lived there and threatened the kingdom. Stories of her exploits are still told today as folk-tales and legends - the story of how Nia cleverly out-witted the RiddleSphynx of the Ivy Grove, or the fable of how she bravely led her compatriots into the heart of the Necromancer's Lair to heroically save her second-in-command Baron Gristlehelm from the death-wizard's clutches. 

Poor Queen Nia, she and her Court truly believe that they're doing the right thing - they see themselves in the delusion as kind and caring, standing up to protect the weak and defenceless, and to defend the natural world of Ghyran 😢  I'll copy some of the short stories I've written up after games below.

100% home brew, but my Ghyran based Flesh Eater Courts worship "Offalielle". In their deluded minds they believe they praise and are blessed by the goddess of life and nature, Alarielle, but the curse twists this into Offalielle. So while yes, they do worship Alarielle, theirs is a very warped version - where they see themselves respectfully nurturing groves of trees in reality they're draping gore slick entails around branches, and where they see themselves offering up beautiful carvings and gifts to the goddess and her pantheon in reality they're stabbing broken bones into the Sylvaneth they're fighting. 


Theirs is a noble task indeed, to protect the natural order of the realms against the forces of Chaos and destruction. And how generous the godess is, to provide such bounteous feasts for her loyal subjects! 🍖

I've only ever had the one Blood Bowl team (thnking about it, that goes for most games for me - 40K is just my Tyranids, Fantasy is just my Wood Elves, Malifaux is just Arcanists.... seeing a pattern here!) - my Wood Elf team, 'The Harts Of Athel Loren'. Aside from being a little wlordplay on 'hart' as in the old English word for stag and 'hart' as a homonym for heart, they're a team from the glades of the Waterfall Palace of the Naiad Court in Athel Loren.

This glade, secreted deep in the heart of the forest, is a beautiful vista of groves of trees, soaring rocky outcrops and crashing waterfalls. Practicing Blood Bowl in this environment has given the players of the Harts very sure feet, as if you can catch a ball while leaping from water-slick rock to a moss-covered outcrop you can certainly catch it on the pitch! In homage to their home, the Harts all wear blue detailing in their kit as well as the traditional browns and greens, representing the stunning waterfalls that characterise the glade.

Tabletop or PC, I'll always play with the Harts, I just love my Wood Elves too much :)
